context:
Matter: a public-records request against the Executive Office of the Governor of Florida, covering email sent
or received by Governor Jeb Bush and his staff during his two terms (1999-2007). The collection is government
email: constituent letters, staff correspondence, press clippings and news forwards, scheduling, legislation
and budget traffic, agency reports, and personal messages. Emails are shown with their headers, as a reviewer
would see them; quoted earlier messages and forwarded articles are part of the document.

Each request names an issue. The requesting party reads every request at the level of the issue, not the
sentence: an email is responsive if it substantively concerns the issue, its background, the policy fights and
legislation around it, or its consequences in Florida, even when the request's exact words never appear. A
constituent asking the Governor to sign or veto a bill on the issue is responsive. A passing use of a word
from the request, with no substantive connection to the issue, is not. Note that "Governor Bush" and "Jeb" in
these emails refer to Jeb Bush, the Governor of Florida, not to his brother the President.
gate_question:
Does this email have substantive content about a matter of Florida state government or public policy (as
opposed to a bare scheduling note, a greeting or thank-you with no subject matter, an empty forward, an
auto-reply, spam, or a purely personal message)?

403.note: Jev (TypeSafe System One), System One request, `base` configuration. In the multi arm all requests of the task go in the same call, as sibling questions over the same state; the state is sent once.

type: noul
instructions: |
  Is this document responsive to the following request for production?

  All documents concerning the extraction of water in Florida for bottling by commercial enterprises.
criteria:
  true: |
    The email concerns commercial extraction of Florida water for bottling, or the protection of the springs and
    groundwater from which it is drawn: bottling companies and their withdrawals; water-use or consumptive-use
    permits for pumping spring or aquifer water; minimum flows and levels for springs; the Springs Initiative and
    Springs Task Force; opposition to pumping or bottling operations; and legislation, fees, or taxes on water
    extraction or bottled water.
  false: |
    The email does not concern water extraction for bottling or the protection of Florida's springs and
    groundwater from withdrawal. Drinking-water quality, drought and water supply for cities, Everglades
    restoration, coastal or surface-water pollution, and bottled water bought or distributed are not responsive.
